content.value_statement: 3D web work can become slow, inaccessible, or hard to plan. This skill guides stack selection, model preparation, scene implementation, performance tuning, and fallbacks.
actual_capabilities: Compare Spline, React Three Fiber, Three.js, and Babylon.js for a 3D web project.
Outline model preparation steps for GLB or GLTF assets, including compression targets.
Provide React Three Fiber scene patterns with loading states, controls, and fallbacks.
Suggest scroll-driven 3D patterns using React Three Fiber or GSAP.
Review 3D performance targets for desktop, mobile, and low-end devices.
Define validation checks for loading indicators, WebGL fallbacks, model optimization, controls, and DPR.
limitations: Does not generate or inspect 3D assets by itself.
Requires project-specific testing on real devices for frame rate, memory, and WebGL support.
Example commands and package installs need user review before execution.
Does not replace licensing review for external models, textures, or Spline scenes.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Configurator
use_cases.description: Select a 3D stack, outline a model pipeline, and define interaction patterns for product variants.

use_cases.title: Optimize an Immersive Portfolio
use_cases.description: Review scene complexity, loading behavior, mobile fallbacks, and scroll-driven animation choices.

use_cases.title: Add 3D to a React App
use_cases.description: Choose React Three Fiber patterns for models, controls, lazy loading, and WebGL fallback states.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a 3D Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between Spline, React Three Fiber, Three.js, and Babylon.js for this web project: [describe project, team, timeline, and interaction needs].

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Web Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 3D model preparation plan for a web scene using these assets: [asset types, sizes, target devices, and visual quality goals].

prompt_templates.title: Design an R3F Scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a React Three Fiber scene plan for [feature]. Include loading states, controls, fallback behavior, and performance constraints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit 3D Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this 3D web experience for performance and usability: [describe scene, device targets, asset sizes, interactions, and current problems].

output_examples.input: I need a product color configurator for a React storefront.
output: Recommended stack: React Three Fiber with drei controls and compressed GLB assets.
Implementation plan: prepare variants, add material switching, add loading UI, and include static fallback images.
Validation plan: test mobile frame rate, touch controls, loading time, and product image parity.

output_examples.input: Our mobile 3D landing page drops frames during scroll.
output: Primary risks: high DPR, heavy model geometry, too many lights, and scroll controls competing with touch input.
Suggested fixes: lower mobile DPR, compress textures, simplify lighting, and disable zoom during page scroll.
Acceptance checks: stable 30 frames per second on target phones and usable static fallback content.

output_examples.input: Should I use Spline or Three.js for a quick hero scene?
output_examples.output: Use Spline for a fast visual prototype with limited custom logic. Use Three.js or React Three Fiber when you need deep control, complex state, or custom shaders.

best_practices: Set performance targets by device class before designing scene complexity.
Use compressed GLB assets and static fallbacks for unsupported devices.
Test loading states, controls, touch behavior, and frame rate on real hardware.
anti_patterns: Shipping large uncompressed models without a loading state.
Using OrbitControls in pages where scroll or touch gestures are primary navigation.
Adding 3D solely for decoration when it slows the main workflow.

faq.question: Can this skill help choose between Spline and React Three Fiber?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common 3D web stacks by speed, control, complexity, and project fit.

faq.question: Does it create 3D models?
faq.answer: No. It guides model preparation, format choices, compression, loading, and integration into web scenes.

faq.question: Can it improve mobile 3D performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers DPR limits, triangle budgets, compressed assets, lighting choices, and fallback strategies.

faq.question: Does it support product configurators?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan stack choices, variant interactions, model pipelines, and mobile validation for configurators.

faq.question: Will it run package installation commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. Commands are examples. Users should review and approve package installation before execution.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility fallbacks?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends loading states, WebGL fallbacks, static previews, and usable non-3D alternatives.
